assigned.title: Provider outbound HTTP resolves, classifies and pins its destination
assigned.acceptance: THE CANONICAL HOST AND NETWORK POLICY MOVES TO A DEPENDENCY-LEAF PACKAGE, @liberty/net-policy, and both existing classifiers consume it. This replaces the original design, which was 'provider-sdk adopts media-inspection's resolve-and-pin control'; that is preserved in acceptanceOriginal and is NOT to be implemented. WHY THE DESIGN CHANGED, because the reason is the whole point: PL-0709 had to import provider-sdk's classifyHost from media-inspection BY DEEP RELATIVE PATH to write its agreement test, since classifyHost is not exported from packages/provider-sdk/src/index.ts and that package's exports field is a bare ./src/index.ts with no subpaths. The reviewer accepted that import FOR THAT TEST ONLY AT THAT TREE and ruled it is not an acceptable permanent boundary. Making media-inspection depend on provider-sdk, or provider-sdk on media-inspection while media-inspection imports provider-sdk to compare, CREATES OR INVITES A WORKSPACE DEPENDENCY CYCLE -- PL-0710 has provider-sdk adopting media-inspection's authoriseFetchTarget, so the arrow already points the other way. A lower shared layer with NO dependency on provider-sdk or media-inspection is the shape that works. REQUIRED, extraction half: the canonical host and IP classification vocabulary and its normalisation move into @liberty/net-policy; provider-sdk consumes that shared classifier; media-inspection consumes that shared classifier; PL-0709's deep cross-package test import is REMOVED; and the agreement test becomes unnecessary as two implementations become one -- replace it with tests of the shared classifier PLUS package-boundary tests proving both consumers actually import it, because an extraction nothing imports is a third copy rather than a merge. The package name may follow repository convention, but the package must be a dependency leaf. REQUIRED, resolve-and-pin half, unchanged from the original and each clause a separate way host-literal checking fails: DNS resolution before the outbound connection; EVERY resolved address classified, not just the first; refusal if ANY resolved address is private, loopback, link-local or reserved, unless an explicitly permitted local-only path applies; the connection PINNED to the approved resolved address so DNS rebinding cannot change the destination between check and connect; resolution, classification and pinning repeated PER REDIRECT HOP; and TLS CERTIFICATE HOSTNAME VERIFICATION AND SNI REMAIN AGAINST THE ORIGINAL HOSTNAME, NOT THE PINNED IP -- pinning the transport must not turn into verifying the wrong name. Regressions required for public-name-to-private-IP, DNS rebinding, mixed public and private answer sets, and translated-address cases. ALSO IN SCOPE BECAUSE THE EXTRACTION PUTS IT IN PLAY: pin.ts's normaliseHost does not fold the DNS root label. It is safe today because both sides of that comparison come from the same URL object so they carry or omit the dot together, and a mismatch refuses the connection -- but it is a third canonicaliser, and this is the task that removes the others. WHY THIS IS P0: F1, F7 and F8 were three host spellings in one function, and F12 was a fourth spelling in a SECOND function written specifically to avoid duplicating the first. The duplication got in anyway -- not as a copied classifier but as a copied assumption about what a hostname string is. A check comparing a string against literals is only ever as complete as the list of spellings whoever wrote it thought of; resolve-and-pin classifies the address a resolver returned, which has one spelling. FOLDED IN 2026-09-20 from the PL-0305 handoff's remaining off-surface item, because this task already owns both packages and the packaging metadata: @liberty/media-inspection's exports field has no ./http subpath, so importing @liberty/catalog-ingestion from apps/web pulls hls.ts into the program and needs an ambient m3u8-parser shim reached by a triple-slash reference in the ingestion package's index. That reference is the smallest honest fix from inside that package and is not the fix. THE SAME DEFECT SHAPE AS THE ONE THIS TASK EXISTS FOR: provider-sdk's classifyHost is unreachable from outside its package for exactly the same reason, a bare ./src/index.ts exports field with no subpaths, which is why PL-0709 had to import it by deep relative path. Give @liberty/media-inspection the subpath exports its consumers actually need and remove the triple-slash workaround, and make sure @liberty/net-policy is published with the subpaths ITS two consumers need rather than repeating the omission in the new package.

THE TYPECHECK IS THE DELIVERABLE HERE RATHER THAN A SIDE CONDITION, and the red-then-green is a typecheck: with the relocated reference removed from packages/media-inspection/src/hls.ts, apps/web fails as 'hls.ts(1,24): error TS7016: Could not find a declaration file for module m3u8-parser'; restored, apps/web exits 0. packages/catalog-ingestion also exits 0 with its own triple-slash reference gone.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force, exit 0, 20 of 20, 0 cached, 2644 passed 1 skipped (2642 before this corrective; +2 is the new regression pair). npm run test:scripts 0, npm run repo:validate 0. THE REGRESSION IS MUTATION-CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is what it is for: removing the reference from hls.ts fails with 'expected import { Parser } from "m3u8-parser"; to be /// <reference path="./m3u8-parser.d.ts" />'; re-adding a downstream reference in catalog-ingestion instead fails the other assertion with 'expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []'. So the guard pins the property AND the consequence the property exists for, and neither half passes while the other is violated.

assigned.acceptanceOriginal: Provider outbound HTTP adopts the existing @liberty/media-inspection resolve-and-pin control (authoriseFetchTarget / nodePinnedFetch) instead of classifying host literals. Required, and each clause is a separate way host-literal checking fails: DNS resolution happens BEFORE the outbound connection; EVERY resolved address is classified, not just the first; the request is refused if ANY resolved address is private, loopback, link-local or reserved, unless an explicitly permitted local-only path applies; the connection is PINNED to the approved resolved address, so DNS rebinding cannot change the destination between the check and the connect; redirects repeat resolution, classification and pinning PER HOP; and TLS hostname verification and SNI are not regressed -- pinning to an address must still present and verify the name. Tests are required for public-name-to-private-IP, DNS rebinding, mixed public/private answer sets, and translation-prefix cases. WHY THIS IS P0 AND WHY IT IS FILED NOW: F1, F7 and F8 are three defects of ONE SHAPE in one function -- a host spelling the string comparisons did not anticipate, each reading as public, none findable by reading. A check that compares a string against literals is only ever as complete as the list of spellings whoever wrote it thought of. Resolve-and-pin classifies the address a resolver returned, which has one spelling.
assigned.architectureAmendedBeforeClaim: AMENDED 2026-09-19 BY gpt-architect's explicit round-50 direction, BEFORE THE CLAIM, and the reviewer was equally explicit that it must be done before rather than after: 'Amend PL-0710's allowedPaths BEFORE CLAIM to include the new shared package and the minimum workspace/package metadata needed to create it. Do not widen it after implementation has already started.' The surface accordingly grew from ['packages/provider-sdk/**','docs/SECURITY.md'] to include packages/net-policy/** (the new leaf package), packages/media-inspection/** (the second consumer, and the home of the deep import being removed), and the minimum workspace metadata: package.json and package-lock.json because npm workspaces is 'apps/*, packages/*' and a new package needs the lockfile regenerated, tsconfig.base.json for path mapping, turbo.json for the pipeline, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md because a new package in the dependency graph is an architecture fact. THIS IS A WIDE SURFACE AND IT IS RESERVED BEFORE THE WORK STARTS ON PURPOSE -- an extraction that discovers its consumers mid-flight is exactly the case the no-widening-after-start rule exists for.
assigned.surfaceCorrectedBeforeClaim: CORRECTED 2026-09-20, BEFORE THE CLAIM: root package.json REMOVED from allowedPaths. I declared it in the round-50 amendment as 'the minimum workspace metadata needed to create the package', and that was a guess rather than a finding. THE EVIDENCE SAYS IT IS NOT NEEDED: root package.json declares workspaces as the pure globs ['apps/*','packages/*'], so packages/net-policy is picked up with no edit; it has no script naming any package path and no @liberty dependency; and tsconfig.base.json carries NO compilerOptions.paths at all, so there is no path map to extend either -- packages resolve through the workspace links. package-lock.json, which genuinely must be regenerated, stays. BOTH FACTS ARE TRUE AND BOTH ARE STATED, because only one of them is a good reason: the entry was unnecessary, AND it was the single path blocking this P0, because PL-AI-0008 has declared root package.json since round 47 and has sat in REVIEW without a verdict since. Removing a needed path to dodge a reservation is the move this project does not make; removing an unneeded one I declared speculatively is correcting my own over-declaration, and the right time to do it is before the claim rather than after. FLAGGED TO THE REVIEWER RATHER THAN TREATED AS SETTLED -- if gpt-architect reads this as manufacturing readiness, the entry goes back and PL-0710 waits for PL-AI-0008. THE IMPLEMENTER IS INSTRUCTED THAT IF ROOT package.json TURNS OUT TO BE NEEDED, IT MUST STOP AND SAY SO rather than reach for it, because a widening after implementation starts is what the round-50 amendment forbade.

review.evidence: CHANGES_REQUESTED, NARROW CORRECTIVE ONLY. security-review PASS and rights-review PASS: the substantive security architecture is ACCEPTED -- @liberty/net-policy is the shared lower-layer host and address vocabulary rather than another copy in either consumer; provider-sdk and media-inspection both consume it; the provider path resolves before connect and classifies EVERY returned address; private, loopback, link-local and reserved answers fail according to the established local-only policy; authorised addresses travel into the pinned transport rather than being re-resolved at connect; redirects repeat validation, resolution and pinning per hop; the transport preserves the ORIGINAL HOSTNAME for Host, SNI and certificate identity rather than verifying the pinned IP; the old unpinned global fetch fallback is no longer the provider transport shape; media-inspection publishes the required ./http subpath; and the reported surviving mutants do not invalidate the accepted security property because they were EXPLICITLY RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. BLOCKING ACCEPTANCE MISS: packages/catalog-ingestion/src/index.ts still begins with the triple-slash reference to ../../media-inspection/src/m3u8-parser.d.ts, and PL-0710's folded acceptance explicitly requires removing that workaround once @liberty/media-inspection/http is available. The comment immediately following it is now stale too -- it says media-inspection publishes one entry point and that ./http is still the future fix, which PL-0710 itself has already made false. DO NOT REDESIGN THE ACCEPTED RESOLVE-AND-PIN IMPLEMENTATION; the corrective is packaging-boundary cleanup only. TRANSCRIBED BY CLAUDE from the review relayed by the human commander.

assigned.surfaceWidenedOnReview: WIDENED 2026-09-21 BY THE REVIEWER'S CHANGES_REQUESTED, which granted EXACTLY ONE PATH and said why it is not speculative: 'PL-0710's acceptance requires this corrective but its current allowedPaths omitted packages/catalog-ingestion/src/index.ts. Amend PL-0710's allowedPaths by adding EXACTLY packages/catalog-ingestion/src/index.ts. This is reviewer-authorized because it is the file explicitly named by the pre-existing folded acceptance. It is not a speculative surface expansion.' One path, named by the reviewer, added verbatim -- not the package, not a glob, not the tsconfig. THE MISS IS MINE TO OWN: the ./http subpath item was folded into this task's acceptance in round 52 precisely BECAUSE the triple-slash workaround lives in that file, and I then declared a surface that could not reach it. The part-A implementer did the media-inspection half, stopped at the boundary and said in its report that removing the reference needed a path it did not have; I recorded that as an out-of-surface note in the handoff instead of correcting the declaration, which is how an acceptance clause survived two gate runs unsatisfied. I BRIEFLY ADDED A SECOND PATH AND THEN TOOK IT BACK OUT, AND THE REASON IS WORTH MORE THAN THE EDIT. Removing the reference from index.ts alone left apps/web failing with 'hls.ts(1,24): error TS7016: Could not find a declaration file for module m3u8-parser', because transport.ts ALSO imports the root barrel and the barrel re-exports ./hls. So I added transport.ts. That did not fix it either -- wikidata.ts and provider.ts import the root as well, so the grant of one file was really a request for four, and I was revising my own justification upward each time I found another. THAT IS THE PATTERN TO STOP ON, so I reverted both catalog-ingestion files and looked for the fix inside the surface I already had. IT WAS THERE. The ambient m3u8-parser declaration was being referenced from a DOWNSTREAM CONSUMER'S BARREL instead of from the file that needs it; putting the triple-slash reference on packages/media-inspection/src/hls.ts itself makes it travel with the import it supplies types for, and apps/web then typechecks with catalog-ingestion COMPLETELY UNTOUCHED. Verified: apps/web tsc exit 0. The granted single path is now sufficient for what it was granted for, and the reviewer's 'EXACTLY' stands unbroken.
